lemma chartPairCoverData_pieces_inl (j : Fin (chartPairCoverData C R π).m₀) :

@[simp]
lemma chartPairCoverData_pieces_inr (j : Fin (chartPairCoverData C R π).m₁) :
    (chartPairCoverData C R π).pieces (Sum.inr j)
      = (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ := by
  rw [FinCoverData.pieces_inr]
  exact (relCurve C R).basicOpen_one

/-- Every piece of the coarse cover data is one of the two pinned charts. -/
lemma chartPairCoverData_pieces_eq (j : (chartPairCoverData C R π).index) :
    (chartPairCoverData C R π).pieces j = (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀
      ∨ (chartPairCoverData C R π).pieces j = (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ := by
  cases j with
  | inl j => exact Or.inl (chartPairCoverData_pieces_inl C R π j)
  | inr j => exact Or.inr (chartPairCoverData_pieces_inr C R π j)

namespace DivisorAdaptation

variable {C R π} {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}

/-- **The coarse adaptation from a chart-principality datum.** `pt` names, for each pinned
chart, a member of `d`'s cover containing that whole chart; `eqn` is the chart equation and
`unit` the comparison unit against `d`'s equation there.  The result is an adaptation whose
two pieces are the pinned charts themselves. -/
noncomputable def ofChartPair
    (eqn : ∀ j : (chartPairCoverData C R π).index,
      Γ(relCurve C R, (chartPairCoverData C R π).pieces j))
    (pt : (chartPairCoverData C R π).index → relCurve C R)
    (piece_le : ∀ j, (chartPairCoverData C R π).pieces j ≤ d.cover.opens (pt j))
    (unit : ∀ j, Γ(relCurve C R, (chartPairCoverData C R π).pieces j)ˣ)
    (eqn_eq : ∀ j, eqn j
      = (unit j : Γ(relCurve C R, (chartPairCoverData C R π).pieces j))
        * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE (piece_le j)).op).hom (d.eqn (pt j))) :
    DivisorAdaptation C R π d :=
  DivisorAdaptation.ofAnchors (chartPairCoverData C R π) eqn pt piece_le unit eqn_eq

/-- **The pieces of `ofChartPair` are the pinned charts.** The anchored constructor keeps the
supplied cover data, so this is definitional plus `Scheme.basicOpen_one`. -/
lemma ofChartPair_pieces_eq_chart
    (eqn : ∀ j : (chartPairCoverData C R π).index,
      Γ(relCurve C R, (chartPairCoverData C R π).pieces j))
    (pt : (chartPairCoverData C R π).index → relCurve C R)
    (piece_le : ∀ j, (chartPairCoverData C R π).pieces j ≤ d.cover.opens (pt j))
    (unit : ∀ j, Γ(relCurve C R, (chartPairCoverData C R π).pieces j)ˣ)
    (eqn_eq : ∀ j, eqn j
      = (unit j : Γ(relCurve C R, (chartPairCoverData C R π).pieces j))
        * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE (piece_le j)).op).hom (d.eqn (pt j)))
    (j : (ofChartPair eqn pt piece_le unit eqn_eq).index) :
    (ofChartPair eqn pt piece_le unit eqn_eq).pieces j
        = (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀
      ∨ (ofChartPair eqn pt piece_le unit eqn_eq).pieces j
        = (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ :=
  chartPairCoverData_pieces_eq C R π j

/-! ## The certificate obligations for a chart-shaped adaptation

Stated against the *shape* of the pieces rather than against `ofChartPair` itself, so that any
adaptation whose pieces are the two pinned charts — however it was built — qualifies. -/

variable (A : DivisorAdaptation C R π d)

/-- **A divisor inside the chart overlap is swallowed by every chart-shaped piece.** -/
theorem forall_subset_or_disjoint_of_pieces_eq_chart
    (hpieces : ∀ j : A.index, A.pieces j = (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀
      ∨ A.pieces j = (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁)
    (hsub : d.supportLocus ⊆ (((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀
      ⊓ (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ : (relCurve C R).Opens) : Set (relCurve C R))) :
    ∀ j : A.index, d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
      ∨ Disjoint d.supportLocus (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R)) := by
  intro j
  refine Or.inl fun x hx => ?_
  have hx' := hsub hx
  rcases hpieces j with h | h <;> rw [h]
  · exact hx'.1
  · exact hx'.2

/-- **The assembler's `hnoLeak` for a chart-shaped adaptation of a chart-overlap divisor.** No
fibre, no tube, no packet idempotent. -/
theorem forall_noLeak_of_pieces_eq_chart
    (hpieces : ∀ j : A.index, A.pieces j = (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀
      ∨ A.pieces j = (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁)
    (hsub : d.supportLocus ⊆ (((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀
      ⊓ (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ : (relCurve C R).Opens) : Set (relCurve C R))) :
    ∀ (j : A.index) (s : Spec (.of R)),
      ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (.of R)).base ⁻¹' {s}
          ∩ closure (d.supportLocus ∩ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) ⊆
        (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R)) :=
  A.forall_noLeak_of_forall_subset_or_disjoint
    (A.forall_subset_or_disjoint_of_pieces_eq_chart hpieces hsub)

section Finite

variable [IsProper C.hom]

/-- **Clause (c1)-finite for a chart-shaped adaptation of a chart-overlap divisor.** -/
theorem forall_finite_colength_of_pieces_eq_chart
    (hpieces : ∀ j : A.index, A.pieces j = (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀
      ∨ A.pieces j = (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁)
    (hsub : d.supportLocus ⊆ (((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀
      ⊓ (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ : (relCurve C R).Opens) : Set (relCurve C R))) :
    ∀ j : A.index, Module.Finite R (A.colength j) :=
  A.forall_finite_colength_of_forall_subset_or_disjoint
    (A.forall_subset_or_disjoint_of_pieces_eq_chart hpieces hsub)

end Finite

end DivisorAdaptation

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivSchemeCertZarConn

/-!
# The coarse adaptation: one piece per pinned chart

`DivSchemeCertZarConn.lean` decides which divisors the certificate interface can see at all:
a connected one must lie inside a single pinned chart.  This file supplies the adaptation to
use once that holds, and it is the coarsest one possible — **one piece per chart, the chart
itself**.

`FinCoverData` asks for a partition of unity on each pinned chart; taking a single generator
`h = 1` with coefficient `a = 1` satisfies it trivially, and `Scheme.basicOpen_one` identifies
the resulting piece with the chart.  Feeding that cover data to the landed anchored
constructor `DivisorAdaptation.ofAnchors` turns a *chart-principality* datum — one member of
`d`'s cover containing each pinned chart, with a comparison unit — into an adaptation whose
two pieces are `V₀` and `V₁`.

For that adaptation the certificate's per-piece obligations are as small as they can be:

* if `supportLocus ⊆ V₀ ⊓ V₁` then **both** pieces swallow the support, so `hnoLeak` and
  clause (c1)-finite hold at every piece (`DivSchemeCertZarSwallow.lean`), with no fibre
  analysis and no packet idempotent;
* none of the landed no-gos touches this configuration.  `not_exists_unique_support_piece`
  refutes *one* support-meeting piece and this adaptation has *two*;
  `supportLocus_disjoint_chart_inter_of_separated` refutes *separation* and this adaptation is
  as unseparated as possible — its two pieces share the whole overlap.

The residual hypothesis, chart principality, is the honest one: it says the divisor is cut by
a single equation on each pinned chart, i.e. it is the statement that the DD-R window's local
generators can be taken globally on a chart.  The pointwise gate
(`isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_exists_certified_adaptation`) licenses shrinking the base
before asking for it.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.chartPairCoverData` — the two-piece cover data, one piece per pinned
  chart, with `pieces_inl`/`pieces_inr` identifying the pieces with `V₀` and `V₁`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.ofChartPair` — the adaptation from a chart-principality
  datum.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.ofChartPair_pieces_eq_chart` — its pieces are the
  pinned charts.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.forall_subset_or_disjoint_of_pieces_eq_chart` — a
  divisor inside the chart overlap is swallowed by every chart-shaped piece.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.forall_noLeak_of_pieces_eq_chart` and
  `forall_finite_colength_of_pieces_eq_chart` — the assembler's `hnoLeak` and clause
  (c1)-finite for a chart-shaped adaptation of a chart-overlap divisor.
-/

def unitLocus : X.Opens := ⨆ x, X.basicOpen (d.eqn x)

lemma basicOpen_le_unitLocus (x : X) : X.basicOpen (d.eqn x) ≤ d.unitLocus :=
  le_iSup (fun x => X.basicOpen (d.eqn x)) x

/-- Membership in the unit locus reads on ANY covering member containing the point:
`y ∈ unitLocus` iff the germ of `eqn x` at `y` is a unit, for every member `x` with
`y ∈ cover.opens x` (well-definedness across members is the ratio law). -/
lemma mem_unitLocus_iff_isUnit_germ {x y : X} (hy : y ∈ d.cover.opens x) :
    y ∈ d.unitLocus
      ↔ IsUnit ((X.presheaf.germ (d.cover.opens x) y hy).hom (d.eqn x)) := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    obtain ⟨x', hx'⟩ := Opens.mem_iSup.mp h
    have hy' : y ∈ d.cover.opens x' := X.basicOpen_le _ hx'
    have hu' : IsUnit ((X.presheaf.germ (d.cover.opens x') y hy').hom (d.eqn x')) :=
      (X.mem_basicOpen _ y hy').mp hx'
    obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := d.ratio_isUnit x x'
    have hyW : y ∈ d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens x' := ⟨hy, hy'⟩
    have h := congrArg
      ((X.presheaf.germ (d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens x') y hyW).hom) hu
    rw [map_mul, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply] at h
    rw [h, IsUnit.mul_iff]
    exact ⟨u.isUnit.map _, hu'⟩
  · intro h
    exact Opens.mem_iSup.mpr ⟨x, (X.mem_basicOpen _ y hy).mpr h⟩

/-- **The support locus** of a local-equation system: the closed set of points where
the (well-defined) germ of the local equation fails to be a unit — the underlying set
of the divisor cut by `d`. -/
def supportLocus : Set X := (d.unitLocus : Set X)ᶜ

lemma isClosed_supportLocus : IsClosed d.supportLocus :=
  d.unitLocus.isOpen.isClosed_compl

lemma mem_supportLocus_iff_not_isUnit_germ {x y : X} (hy : y ∈ d.cover.opens x) :
    y ∈ d.supportLocus
      ↔ ¬ IsUnit ((X.presheaf.germ (d.cover.opens x) y hy).hom (d.eqn x)) :=
  not_congr (d.mem_unitLocus_iff_isUnit_germ hy)

/-- **The per-member trace of the support**: on a covering member, the support locus is
the member minus the basic open of its equation. -/
lemma supportLocus_inter_opens (x : X) :
    d.supportLocus ∩ (d.cover.opens x : Set X)
      = (d.cover.opens x : Set X) \ (X.basicOpen (d.eqn x) : Set X) := by
  ext y
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨hsupp, hy⟩
    refine ⟨hy, fun hyb => hsupp (d.basicOpen_le_unitLocus x hyb)⟩
  · rintro ⟨hy, hyb⟩

9	/-!
10	# Swallow or miss: the shape of an adaptation that can be certified
11	
12	`DivSchemeCertZarChartTrace.lean` shows that the assembler's per-piece no-leak clause
13	*forces* the chart traces `supportLocus ∩ V_b` to be closed.  This file gives the matching
14	sufficient condition, and it is deliberately crude:
15	
16	> if every piece either **swallows** the support (`supportLocus ⊆ pieces j`) or **misses**
17	> it (`Disjoint supportLocus (pieces j)`), then no-leak holds at every piece.
18	
19	For a swallowing piece the trace is the whole support, which is closed by construction
20	(`isClosed_supportLocus`); for a missing piece the trace is empty.  Neither case needs a
21	fibre, a tube, or an idempotent.
22	
23	The crudeness is not a defect, because the necessity lemma pins down exactly how much
24	freedom is left.  Both pinned charts are covered by their pieces, so
25	
26	* if some chart-`b` piece meets the support it must swallow it, whence `supportLocus ⊆ V_b`;
27	* otherwise every chart-`b` piece misses the support, whence `supportLocus ∩ V_b = ∅`.
28	
29	Since `V₀ ⊔ V₁` is the whole relative curve, a nonempty support therefore lies in
30	`V₀ ⊓ V₁` — the divisor must avoid **both** vertical fibres `pi⁻¹(0)` and `pi⁻¹(∞)` — or be
31	confined to one of them.  That is the honest chart-design hypothesis of the lane, and it is
32	where the DD-R atlas has to do its work; it is not something a support tube, a packet
33	idempotent, or a shrink of the base can manufacture.
34	
35	A missing piece contributes nothing at all: its equation is a unit, so its colength module
36	vanishes (`subsingleton_colength_of_disjoint_supportLocus`) and clauses (c1) hold there for
37	free — no fibrewise regularity input.  So the certificate of a swallow-or-miss adaptation is
38	carried entirely by the swallowing pieces, at most one per chart.
39	
40	## Main declarations
41	
42	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.subsingleton_colength_of_disjoint_supportLocus` — a
43	  piece missing the support has a vanishing colength.
44	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.supportLeak_eq_empty_of_subset_or_disjoint` — swallow
45	  or miss gives no-leak at that piece.
46	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.forall_noLeak_of_forall_subset_or_disjoint` — the
47	  assembler-shaped `hnoLeak`, with no fibre analysis.
48	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.forall_finite_colength_of_forall_subset_or_disjoint` —
49	  clause (c1)-finite at every piece.
50	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.subset_chart₀_or_disjoint_chart₀` /
51	  `…_chart₁_…` — the design constraint the shape imposes on the divisor.
52	-/

76	
77	/-- **A piece that misses the support has a vanishing colength.** Its equation has a unit
78	germ at every point of the piece (`isUnit_germ_eqn_iff` read through the unit locus), hence

82	such a piece the certificate's clauses (c1) are free, with no fibrewise regularity input. -/
83	lemma subsingleton_colength_of_disjoint_supportLocus (j : A.index)
84	    (hdisj : ∀ z : relCurve C R, z ∈ A.pieces j → z ∉ d.supportLocus) :
85	    Subsingleton (A.colength j) := by
86	  have hunit : IsUnit (A.eqn j) := by
87	    apply (relCurve C R).toRingedSpace.isUnit_of_isUnit_germ
88	    intro z hz
89	    have hU : z ∈ d.unitLocus := not_not.mp (hdisj z hz)
90	    exact (A.isUnit_germ_eqn_iff j hz).mpr
91	      ((d.mem_unitLocus_iff_isUnit_germ (d.cover.mem_opens z)).mp hU)

95	/-! ## Swallow or miss gives no-leak -/

104	  refine (d.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_iff_supportLeak_eq_empty (A.pieces j)).mp ?_

106	  · rw [Set.inter_eq_left.mpr hsub]
107	    exact d.isClosed_supportLocus
108	  · rw [Set.disjoint_iff_inter_eq_empty.mp hdisj]
109	    exact isClosed_empty

113	`isCertified_of_noLeak_of_forall_liftQ_injective` /

117	      ∨ Disjoint d.supportLocus (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) :
118	    ∀ (j : A.index) (s : Spec (.of R)),

121	        (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R)) := by
122	  intro j s x hx
123	  have hleak := A.supportLeak_eq_empty_of_subset_or_disjoint j (h j)
124	  by_contra hxU
125	  exact Set.eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem.mp hleak x ⟨hx.2, hxU⟩

127	section Finite
128	
129	/- The finiteness engine consumes the properness licence on the relative curve
130	(`instIsProperRelCurveHom`), so this clause — and only this clause — needs `IsProper`. -/
131	variable [IsProper C.hom]
132	
133	/-- **Clause (c1)-finite at every piece, from swallow-or-miss.** -/
134	theorem forall_finite_colength_of_forall_subset_or_disjoint
135	    (h : ∀ j : A.index, d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
136	      ∨ Disjoint d.supportLocus (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) :
137	    ∀ j : A.index, Module.Finite R (A.colength j) := fun j =>
138	  A.finite_colength_of_supportLeak_eq_empty j
139	    (A.supportLeak_eq_empty_of_subset_or_disjoint j (h j))
140	
141	end Finite

143	/-! ## What the shape forces on the divisor
144	
145	The necessity direction of `DivSchemeCertZarChartTrace.lean` is sharpened here: because the
146	chart-`b` pieces cover `V_b`, a swallow-or-miss adaptation exists only for a divisor that is
147	either inside a pinned chart or disjoint from it.  Combined with `V₀ ⊔ V₁ = ⊤` this says a
148	nonempty support lies in `V₀ ⊓ V₁`, or is confined to one vertical fibre of `pi`.
149	
150	This is the statement the DD-R atlas owes: **the chart's divisors avoid `pi⁻¹(0)` and
151	`pi⁻¹(∞)`.**  It is a hypothesis about the chart, and it is the only remaining geometric
152	input of the (c1) side of the certificate. -/
153	
154	/-- **Chart-0 dichotomy.** A swallow-or-miss adaptation forces the support either inside the
155	pinned chart `V₀` or disjoint from it. -/
156	theorem subset_chart₀_or_disjoint_chart₀
157	    (h : ∀ j : A.index, d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
158	      ∨ Disjoint d.supportLocus (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) :
159	    d.supportLocus ⊆ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ : Set (relCurve C R))
160	      ∨ Disjoint d.supportLocus
161	        ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ : Set (relCurve C R)) := by
162	  by_cases hmeet : ∃ j : Fin A.m₀, d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces (Sum.inl j) : Set (relCurve C R))
163	  · obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ := hmeet
164	    exact Or.inl (hj.trans fun x hx => (relCurve C R).basicOpen_le (A.h₀ j) hx)
165	  · refine Or.inr (Set.disjoint_iff_inter_eq_empty.mpr ?_)
166	    rw [A.supportLocus_inter_chart₀_eq_iUnion]
167	    refine Set.iUnion_eq_empty.mpr fun j => Set.disjoint_iff_inter_eq_empty.mp ?_
168	    exact (h (Sum.inl j)).resolve_left fun hsub => hmeet ⟨j, hsub⟩
169	
170	/-- **Chart-1 dichotomy.** -/
171	theorem subset_chart₁_or_disjoint_chart₁
172	    (h : ∀ j : A.index, d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
173	      ∨ Disjoint d.supportLocus (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))) :
174	    d.supportLocus ⊆ ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ : Set (relCurve C R))
175	      ∨ Disjoint d.supportLocus
176	        ((relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ : Set (relCurve C R)) := by
177	  by_cases hmeet : ∃ j : Fin A.m₁, d.supportLocus ⊆ (A.pieces (Sum.inr j) : Set (relCurve C R))
178	  · obtain ⟨j, hj⟩ := hmeet
179	    exact Or.inl (hj.trans fun x hx => (relCurve C R).basicOpen_le (A.h₁ j) hx)
180	  · refine Or.inr (Set.disjoint_iff_inter_eq_empty.mpr ?_)
181	    rw [A.supportLocus_inter_chart₁_eq_iUnion]
182	    refine Set.iUnion_eq_empty.mpr fun j => Set.disjoint_iff_inter_eq_empty.mp ?_
183	    exact (h (Sum.inr j)).resolve_left fun hsub => hmeet ⟨j, hsub⟩
184	
185	end DivisorAdaptation

Base directory for this skill: /home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.claude/skills/horizon-inbox

The inbox is the durable channel between the human, agent sessions (present and
future), and other projects. Act on it through the CLI; never edit inbox files
by hand. Prefer `--json` whenever reading command output for exact ids or
fields.

## Read

- `horizon inbox list` — read the inbox. Use `--json` when you need exact ids,
  labels, scope, author, audience, timestamps, or comments. Use the list filters
  to narrow without losing the overview: `--to horizon`, `--to human`,
  `--project P`, repeated `--kind K`, repeated `--label L`,
  `--status open`, `--query TEXT`, `--limit N`, and `--comments N`.
- Every inbox command evaluates the full local working set, even when `list` is
  filtered. Treat its advisory warnings as a prompt to review duplicates, stale
  memories, and consumed notices. The CLI never archives automatically because
  only the working agent can decide what is resolved; that agent must make an
  explicit cleanup pass before its final report.
- Labels are the release gate. Local inbox items default to `agent-ready`, which
  means they are visible to agents at run boundaries. Keep that default for
  machine-addressed work, and usually keep it for human-addressed notices too:
  it helps later agents see that the human has already been notified and avoids
  duplicate reports. Use `not-ready`, `rejected`, or no labels only when there is
  a concrete reason agents should not see or act on the item yet.
- Audience says who should read the item: empty/general, `horizon`, `human`,
  `project:<name>`, or a **direct message** to another team: `task:<id>` /
  `run:<id>` (older items may carry the legacy `ground` audience).
  Scope/project says what the item is about.
- Horizon reads general items, items addressed to `horizon`, items addressed
  to its project, and DMs addressed to its own task/run. It should ignore other
  projects' and other teams' addressed items.
- Kinds: `hint` (normal guidance), `issue` (problem to fix/report),
  `protection` (standing constraint / soft freeze), `info` (a notice for the
  human — something you did or noticed they should know, e.g. a renamed project
  or an important change; purely informational, never affects what runs),
  `memory` (durable agent note or dead end).

## Ownership & read-state (your team's inbox)

Each running session is a **team**, and the inbox is shared across teams. Two
lightweight overlays keep it navigable:

- **Ownership** — an item is either *shared with everyone* (the default) or
  *owned by one task* (that team's private inbox — e.g. its own memory). Read your
  team's inbox with `horizon inbox list --mine` (owned-by-you **plus** shared);
  another team's private items don't appear. Own an item to your task with
  `horizon inbox add --mine …` (or `--owner <task-id>`), and `horizon inbox own
  <id> --mine|--owner <task>|--shared` to move an existing one. Owning your
  `--kind memory` notes keeps another team's memory out of your working set.
- **Read-state** — read/unread is **per team**, so a shared item several teams see
  tracks who has read it. `horizon inbox list --unread` is what *you* have not read
  yet; `horizon inbox read <id>` marks it read, and `horizon inbox unread <id>`
  puts it back (e.g. you read it but it still needs action). Combine:
  `horizon inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue — the same signal
  the pre-command synchronizer counts for you.

The reader/owner id is inferred from your session (your task), so you rarely pass
it explicitly.

## Act

Authorship is automatic: every item and comment you create through the CLI is
attributed to your role (normally `horizon`) from the run environment — you do
**not** pass `--author` (a stray `--author work-reviewer` is demoted to the
`agent` metadata, not used as the author, so the author set stays conventional).
If you are a dispatched **subagent**, add `--agent <your-name>` (e.g. `--agent
work-reviewer`) to record your identity; it is stored in metadata and shown
next to the role in the UI, keeping the author itself a clean role. Items and
comments are also auto-tagged with the run/session provenance (a small chip in the
UI); you do not pass this yourself.

New inbox items use a two-part body:

- First paragraph = concise title. Keep it short enough to scan in one UI row
  (aim for under ~100 characters); do not put the full explanation here.
- Second paragraph and later = non-empty description. Put the evidence, impact,
  next action, and relevant ids/files here. The description is **mandatory** — an
  item that is only a title is rejected.

Write bodies and comments in **Markdown**: the dashboard renders it. Use short
paragraphs and `-` bullet lists instead of one wall-of-text paragraph, `**bold**`
for the key claim, and backticks for ids, lemma names, files, and code
(`` `lem:foo` ``, `` `Foo.lean:42` ``). A long unstructured blob is hard to scan.

Do not create an item whose body is only a title. If you need a `[persistent]` or
`[temporary]` tag, put it at the start of the title paragraph and keep the rest
of that paragraph concise.

Before opening a new item, search the open inbox for the same topic using
`horizon inbox list --status open --query "key words" --json` and, when relevant,
`--project P` / `--to R`. If a live item already covers the same issue, do not
open a duplicate: add a comment with the new evidence, or edit the body if the
main description is stale. If you discover an open item is obsolete, already
solved, consumed, or superseded, add a short comment when the reason is not
obvious and then run `horizon inbox archive <id>`.

- `horizon inbox comment <id> --body "..."` — progress note on an item (record
  what you did; not to ask the human for clarification). Do not write your name
  into the comment body; the author is set automatically. Drop a comment at each **key advance**
  while you work an item (a milestone reached, a route ruled out, a blocker hit),
  not only at the end — these comments are the item's visible progress trail.
- **Write comments as mathematics, for a human.** State the key step that
  succeeded in human-readable mathematical language (LaTeX for formulas), naming
  the result and the idea — e.g. "Proved $H^i(X,\mathcal{F})=0$ for $i>\dim X$ by
  reducing to the affine case via Čech cohomology." Mention Lean declaration
  names and file paths only as supporting detail; the substance is the maths, not
  a code changelog. This applies to comments on **roadmap items and tasks** too:
  when a key step lands, record it there in the same mathematical, legible style.
- `horizon inbox archive <id>` — soft-delete: keep the item for the record but
  hide it from the dashboard by default. Use for stale, superseded, consumed, or
  no-longer-key context. Keeping the inbox tidy this way is your job (or the
  janitor subagent's) — prune memory/info so they remain small.
- `horizon inbox complete <id>` — mark an item resolved only when it records work
  you genuinely concluded and want to keep visible outside the archive. Before
  completing, add a short **conclusion comment**: first the mathematical
  conclusion (what was proved/established, in words + LaTeX), then concise
  metadata (runs, approximate LOC, files/declarations involved). A reader should
  grasp the result and how it was concluded without opening the logs.
- `horizon inbox add --body "Short title\n\nDescription with details and next action." [--to R] [--project P] [--persistent|--temporary] [--agent <name> if a subagent]`
  — open a new item.
  - `--to` is the recipient: `horizon`, `human`, `project:<name>`, or a direct
    message to another team `task:<id>` / `run:<id>`.
    Use `--to project:<name>` to message another project (e.g. "I rewrote your
    `foo` declaration more cleanly, you may want it"); use `--to task:<id>` to
    message a specific running team.
  - `--owner <task-id>` / `--mine` keeps the item in one team's inbox instead of
    the shared default.
  - `--project` says what the item is ABOUT (its subject).
  - `--persistent` / `--temporary` just prepend a `[persistent]` / `[temporary]`
    tag to the body.
  - `--pending` labels the item `not-ready` instead of the default `agent-ready`,
    so it stays invisible to agents until a human releases it.
- `horizon inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body "Short memory title\n\nDurable fact, convention, or dead end."` — record a durable
  note / dead end. Memory lives in the inbox, so it is rendered in the "Memory"
  section and a human can prune it like any other item.
- `horizon inbox protect --body "..." [--project P] [--file F] [--declaration D] [--blueprint-node N]`
  — add a semantic standing constraint the Horizon agent must respect (a soft freeze),
  e.g. "do not change the signature of `Foo.bar`". These render as a
  "Protected" section; honour them, including semantic ones. For a target that
  must be mechanically blocked before dispatch, the user uses the config-backed
  `horizon freeze add <file|declaration|blueprint-node> <target>` command instead.

Reading convention: an item tagged `[persistent]` is a standing rule — respect
it every round and keep it open while relevant. `[temporary]` (or untagged) is
one-shot — archive it once consumed. Items in the "Protected" section are never
modified.

variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π]

-- The diagonal components of the two Cech arrows are the SAME map.

# The coarse adaptation: one piece per pinned chart

`DivSchemeCertZarConn.lean` decides which divisors the certificate interface can see at all:
a connected one must lie inside a single pinned chart.  This file supplies the adaptation to
use once that holds, and it is the coarsest one possible — **one piece per chart, the chart
itself**.

`FinCoverData` asks for a partition of unity on each pinned chart; taking a single generator
`h = 1` with coefficient `a = 1` satisfies it trivially, and `Scheme.basicOpen_one` identifies
the resulting piece with the chart.  Feeding that cover data to the landed anchored
constructor `DivisorAdaptation.ofAnchors` turns a *chart-principality* datum — one member of
`d`'s cover containing each pinned chart, with a comparison unit — into an adaptation whose
two pieces are `V₀` and `V₁`.

For that adaptation the certificate's per-piece obligations are as small as they can be:

* if `supportLocus ⊆ V₀ ⊓ V₁` then **both** pieces swallow the support, so `hnoLeak` and
  clause (c1)-finite hold at every piece (`DivSchemeCertZarSwallow.lean`), with no fibre
  analysis and no packet idempotent;
* none of the landed no-gos touches this configuration.  `not_exists_unique_support_piece`
  refutes *one* support-meeting piece and this adaptation has *two*;
  `supportLocus_disjoint_chart_inter_of_separated` refutes *separation* and this adaptation is
  as unseparated as possible — its two pieces share the whole overlap.

The residual hypothesis, chart principality, is the honest one: it says the divisor is cut by
a single equation on each pinned chart, i.e. it is the statement that the DD-R window's local
generators can be taken globally on a chart.  The pointwise gate
(`isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_exists_certified_adaptation`) licenses shrinking the base
before asking for it.

  chart, with `pieces_inl`/`pieces_inr` identifying the pieces with `V₀` and `V₁`.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.ofChartPair` — the adaptation from a chart-principality
  datum.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.ofChartPair_pieces_eq_chart` — its pieces are the
  pinned charts.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.forall_subset_or_disjoint_of_pieces_eq_chart` — a
  divisor inside the chart overlap is swallowed by every chart-shaped piece.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.forall_noLeak_of_pieces_eq_chart` and

        (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R)) :=
